answer: One defence is a burn-to-register registry: each agent must burn 25 tokens to trade. First, it sends the tokens to a burn address and posts the receipt on-chain. Second, the registry mints one non-transferable identity, capped at 100 new identities per day. Third, proven misbehaviour voids that identity, so the attacker must burn 25 more tokens to re-enter. Faking 10,000 agents would burn 250,000 tokens — about $125,000 at $0.50 each — and take 100 days under the cap. Like an oasis guarded in the sable dark, the honest pulse of trade survives because freeloaders cannot flood in for free.
